q: 1. A shear force diagram of a simply supported beam shows constant shear force throughout the span. It is subjected to
options: two concentrated loads spaced at points
explain: A pure applied couple (no other transverse loads) produces a constant shear force with a jump in the moment diagram, but constant SF throughout.

q: 2. The shear force on a beam and the displacement are related by
explain: As per the answer key; the standard beam relation is V = EI·d³y/dx³ (third derivative of deflection).

q: 3. Find the maximum BM induced in a simply supported beam if the beam is subjected to a point load of 4 KN at the centre of beam and span of the beam is 4 m
4. In a simply supported beam subjected to a point load at centre, the maximum bending moment occurs at
explain: For a central point load on a simply supported beam, max BM occurs directly under the load, at mid-span.

q: 5. Find the maximum bending moment in a simply supported beam loaded with a UDL of 2 t/m having span 4m
6. Load required to produce unit deflection is called
explain: Stiffness = load / deflection, i.e. the load needed to produce one unit of deflection.

q: 7. A simply supported beam as shown carries 10 t of load, 2 m from support A and 3 m from support B. What will be the reaction at point B?
explain: RB = (Load × distance from A) / span = (10×2)/5 = 4 t.

q: 8. A simply supported beam of span L carries a uniformly distributed load W. The maximum bending moment, M is:
explain: M_max = WL/8 for a full-span UDL (W = total load) on a simply supported beam.

q: 9. The bending moment at a section tends to bend or deflect the beam and internal stresses resist its bending. The resistance offered by the internal stress to the bending, is called:
explain: The internal normal stress that resists bending action is called bending stress.

q: 10. The magnitude of a shear force at a distance of L/4 from either end of a simply supported beam with load P applied at mid span is equal to:
explain: Between each support and the mid-span load, the shear force stays constant and equal to the support reaction, P/2.

q: 11. Bending moment diagram of a simply supported beam with a point load at the centre of the span is:
explain: BM rises linearly from zero at the supports to a peak under the central point load, forming a triangle.

q: 12. Moment of inertia of an object having rectangular section of 'b' as width and 'd' as depth is given by
explain: Standard formula: I = bd³/12 about the centroidal axis.

q: 13. A cantilever beam is one which is:
options: Fixed at one end and free at other end
Supported on more than two supports
explain: A cantilever has one fully fixed end and one completely free end.

q: 14. A beam is said to be loaded in pure bending when
options: Bending moment and shear force are changing linearly
explain: Pure bending is characterized by a constant bending moment (and correspondingly zero shear force) over the section of interest.

q: 15. If the shear force along a section of a beam is zero, the bending moment at the section is:
explain: Since dM/dx = V, wherever shear force is zero, bending moment reaches a local extremum — commonly the maximum bending moment for typical loading cases.

q: 16. If a cantilever beam of 8 m long has a uniformly distributed load of 2 KN/m throughout the length and a 10 KN point load at the center of beam, find the moment at center:
explain: Only the UDL beyond the center (4 m of it, total 8 kN, acting 2 m from center) contributes: 8×2 = 16 kN-m. The point load, applied exactly at the center, has zero moment arm about that same point.
